newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen says strategy aids long term growth.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen says strategy aids long term growth.

text.p: British electricity generator PowerGen Plc said on Thursday that its strategy to minimise the impact of increasing competition in Britain should support long term growth, as it announced investment in projects overseas.

PowerGen said pretax profits before exceptional items for the year were within expectations at 575 million pounds ($945.9 million), up from 566 million previously, and paid out a dividend of 25.2 pence per share, up from 21 pence.

"The results demonstrate the success of our business strategy in minimising the impact on...profitability of increasing intense competition in the UK electricity market," chairman Ed Wallis said in a statement.

PowerGen said that it had agreed to take significant stakes in two independent power projects planned in Indonesia and Thailand, which will cost in total 1.27 billion pounds and increase the company's international capacity by 34 percent and together with other overseas plans will reinforce earnings growth from the international business beyond 2001.

PowerGen, which was frustrated by the British government in its attempts to buy a regional electricity company (Rec) last year, said it was developing longer term partnerships with Recs to secure channels to sell in the domestic market, which will be freed up to competition in 1998.

PowerGen made no comment on a one-off windfall tax proposed by the new Labour government on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities, unlike its colleague National Power, which said on Wednesday at its annual results that it did not think it should face the tax. ($ = 0.607 British Pounds)
